masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Gremot Mobility: a family-backed motor maker, growing quietly inside India's light-EV supply chain.

subhead.text: A Bangalore builder of low-voltage BLDC motors and controllers, more than doubling revenue on a real, independently-confirmed innovation credential.

p1_engine.eyebrow: A real, confirmed credential and a real growth curve, still finding its customers

blocks.text: Gremot Mobility Private Limited was incorporated in September 2019 in Bangalore, founded by Varun Rajendra Rajamane (Founder & Managing Director since January 2020). Co-director Rajendra Shivappa Rajamane is separately Managing Director of Rajamane Industries Private Limited, an established industrial manufacturing enterprise — a genuine family-industrial backing, not a from-scratch founder story. The company runs on ₹5 crore authorized / ₹3.01 crore paid-up capital.

Revenue grew from roughly ₹74 lakh (FY24) to **₹1.73 crore in FY25 — up 134% year on year**, and the two figures are arithmetically consistent with each other, not a low-base distortion. This is a genuinely small but real and growing revenue base, a meaningfully different story from the flat-or-declining revenue seen in some other companies this batch.

Two real credentials, independently confirmed: Gremot's own profile is live on **msh.meity.gov.in**, the Government of India's MeitY Startup Hub platform, directly verified there. And Gremot placed **2nd at iCreate's EVangelise'21** — a genuine, dated EV-innovation challenge — for 'energy recovery capabilities for EV motors,' winning ₹7.5 lakh in grant funding plus ₹50 lakh in incubation support, confirmed via independent trade press.

The company's own stated vision — 'to be the leading supplier for low voltage motors (<100 Volts) in India' — is honestly labeled as a vision, not a claim of current market position, confirmed via a genuine 2021 exhibitor-directory listing. Separately, a claim that Gremot 'possesses both ARAI and ISO certifications' was checked and **rejected** — no citation was given, and no such certification appears anywhere in the company's own materials or in independent search. No patent or DSIR recognition was found either.
blocks.source: IIEV exhibitor directory (vision statement, confirmed); absence of corroborating evidence for certifications

p2_market.eyebrow: A moderate, real growth market, already home to much larger specialists

insights.point: India's low-voltage electric motor market is **real, if not explosive.**
insights.evidence: Valued at $581.4M in 2024, projected to reach $961.7M by 2033 — a 5.32% CAGR, driven by electric mobility and robotics expanding the application base for compact, high-torque-density, thermally efficient motors.

insights.point: Electric two-wheelers are the **largest single demand pool** for this component category.
insights.evidence: 1.40 million electric two-wheelers sold in FY2025-26 — the segment most likely to absorb Gremot's <100V motor/controller focus.
insights.source: market research on EV motor demand by vehicle class

insights.point: But the field already has **much larger, established specialists.**
insights.evidence: Sona Comstar (a large, listed component maker with a UK-partnered patented powertrain technology), Shakti Pumps (20,000 motors/month production capacity), Compage Automation, and Tsuyo all compete in adjacent or overlapping ranges.

reflect.text: A moderate but real growth market, led by two-wheeler electrification, where Gremot competes as a small, focused specialist against much larger, already-scaled component makers — its edge has to be technical fit and design-in relationships, not scale.

p2_market.sourceNote: Market data: Mobility Foresights, IMARC Group. Competitor landscape: EVreporter, Bauaelectric, MarkNtel Advisors.

p3_opportunities.lede: Three places worth a closer look, each built on the real credentials already confirmed.

items.title: Convert the EVangelise win into named design-ins
items.body: The iCreate credential is real and confirmed. The next proof point is turning it into actual, named OEM design-in relationships that can be pointed to directly, rather than the innovation award standing alone.

items.title: Settle the certification question directly
items.body: No ARAI/ISO/AIS certification could be independently confirmed, and OEM buyers in this segment likely expect some component-level compliance evidence. A clear, honest answer — rather than the currently unresolved claim — removes a credibility gap before it matters.
items.source: This research's own verification attempts, rejected as unconfirmed.

items.title: Benchmark growth against a real production-scale target
items.body: Shakti Pumps' 20,000 motors/month gives a concrete, real production-scale benchmark to plan against as Gremot moves from its R&D stage into sales.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only the company's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Publish one named OEM design-in case study
items.body: Even a single, real, citable customer relationship would do more for credibility than the vision statement alone.

items.title: Get an explicit answer on certification status
items.body: Confirm directly whether any AIS/ARAI-type component testing has been done or is planned, rather than leaving the current unresolved claim hanging.

items.title: Set a concrete production-capacity milestone
items.body: A stated, real target — even well below Shakti Pumps' 20,000/month — would mark the R&D-to-sales transition concretely.

takeaway.text: The growth and the innovation credential are real, and now genuinely verified — a small company doing real work in a market much bigger companies also compete in. **What turns this from a promising R&D story into a business is the same thing every one of these profiles keeps landing on: naming the actual customers, not just the vision.**
